newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian PM vows more money for nuclear workers.
newsitem.headline: Russian PM vows more money for nuclear workers.

text.p: Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin vowed on Friday to provide more money for a top Russian nuclear research centre where a research worker recently died after a radiation accident.

"We must take steps to provide proper funding for the nuclear centre to avoid such incidents in the future," he told reporters during a visit to the Arzamas 16 complex in Sarov, about 400 km (250 miles) southeast of Moscow.

Researcher Alexander Zakharov was conducting a weapons test last month involving a controlled nuclear chain reaction using small amounts of uranium when what officials called "a serious breach of the rules" caused an irregular burst of radiation.
Zakharov died in a Moscow hospital a few days later, becoming the first nuclear accident victim since the Chernobyl disaster in 1986.
Chernomyrdin, who heads a government commission on nuclear weapons, said the results of the investigation into the incident would soon be published.
"But even now I can say that there was a major violation of the security precautions by the researcher," he added.
Workers at Arzamas say that poor financing could lead to more nuclear accidents and Chernomyrdin's visit was partly aimed at reassuring them that more money would be made available.
Russia's nuclear sector, long the pride of Soviet science and accustomed to preferential treatment, is experiencing financial crisis. Most of its underpaid workers have not received money for months.
The head of Sarov's local administration told reporters that they were beginning to receive the money needed to pay off the arrears to the Arzamas workers.
"We have received 68 billion roubles ($11.7 million) to pay salaries for March and April and expect more in the next week or so to pay off arrears for May and June," Gennady Karatayev told reporters.
The total debts owed to the centre's employees amount to around 150 billion roubles.

Karatayev said that in the coming weeks local officials would finish drawing up a programme for further development of the nuclear centre which would then be offered to the government for its approval.
Chernomyrdin held talks with the centre's officials behind closed doors. An unnamed official said the prime minister had been shown new designs for nuclear weapons.
Arzamas, one of only two such nuclear weapons establishments in Russia, is surrounded by barbed wire barriers and security is very tight. It is closed to foreigners.
